dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, looks like we meet again, Tailleferre!

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: #Ah, it's you two! The adventurer and {M#his}{F#her} little assistant. Sorry, I've forgotten your names...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The name's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. Thanks for your help last time, by the way — thanks to you, we managed to use a Conch Harp to play ancient music!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, what brings you here to Petrichor?

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: That's what I wanted to ask you — I'm chasing a rumor, but I suppose adventurers like you might already be well ahead of the game.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rumors? What are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Hmm? Don't you know about the big news out of Petrichor lately...?

choices.text: About how we accidentally saved the world?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Huh? What are you... No, no, I'm talking about the rediscovery of the legendary Faded Castle!

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: The last records of the place are several centuries ago. And here I thought that was what you were here for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that... That might've had something to do with us, sure...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: In that case, I'm sure you know that the castle once belonged to Boethius, yes? The most important musician in Fontaine's history?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Whether it be the operas he wrote, or the ancient Remurian scores he compiled, his works all have a special place in music history.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Surely, a vast wealth of resources can be found at the castle in which he once lived, each an important relic to us in the Musicians' Association.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: As such, I rushed here as soon as I heard the news, trying to secure any important relics before all the adventurers get here.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: But I suppose you were one step ahead of me, eh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Err, what should we tell her? That Boethius is actually a big baddie, who used all that music to do a whole bunch of evil stuff...?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Would knowing the truth sadden her...?)

choices.text: The "Symphony" can no longer be used for evil.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Hmm? What are you two talking about? You haven't already found some ancient scores, have you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, uh, what if... And Paimon's saying "if," Boethius was a really, really nasty guy, would you still want the musical scores he left behind?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Hmm... To be honest, while I'm not sure what you mean specifically by him being "really, really nasty," history has few kinds words for him apart from his music.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: From his romantic opera "The Flying Outlander," we can easily tell that he never gave up on reviving Remuria for so long as he lived, and consequently, saw the newborn Fontaine as an enemy.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: According to historians, he also had a hand in the wars that occurred before Fontaine's founding...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: His musical achievements, however, are a different kettle of fish altogether. There might be false histories in his music, but they retain their value as art.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: And as I see it, these things are all a part of history as well. Even the purest of art can be used to do wrong, and all musicians would do well to remember that.

choices.text: Well, I'm sure you wouldn't use these things for evil.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Haha, I'm just a researcher. I am honored beyond words simply to hear these ancient melodies.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Speaking of which, since chance has seen fit for us to meet here, could I ask you to help me out with something?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: You can consider it payment for the favor from last time!

choices.text: You said you didn't need payment last time...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Hehe, in that case, this is just "help" then, right?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Anyway, as I mentioned earlier, I'm here to look for the famous lost opera, "The Flying Outlander."

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: According to records left by someone named Ruggiero several hundred years back, it should be somewhere within the Faded Castle. Could you help me search for it?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: I imagine you're much better versed in such matters than I, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, since she's asked, {NICKNAME}, and those scores don't have "that power" anymore... We might as well, right?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Alright, I'll take that to mean you've agreed. Hehe, splendid!

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: I'm counting on you, then. I'll wait for you in town in the meantime.

choices.text: I'm gonna need to be paid...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Don't worry, you'll be compensated. I'll have you know that the Musicians' Association isn't some gathering of paupers!

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Hehe, well, it's just my personal opinion.

choices.text: It's going to take some time to explain all this...
About the Great Hypnosis of Petrichor?

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: The scenery here truly is rather excellent. We order many an instrument from this town every year, but this is my first time visiting.

choices.text: Tell me about the music score...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: I'm counting on you, then. I'll wait for you in town in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Hmm, this is... Yes, this is indeed "The Flying Outlander." To think that you actually found it...

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: It can't have been easy, but I was right to put my trust in you, excellent adventurers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, thanks! Still, what are you gonna do with the score? Are you gonna perform it at the Opera Epiclese, maybe make a pile of Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Hmm... Making money is important, but I have no intention of keeping this for my own.

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: This ancient art is part of the common wealth of humanity. As such, I will release "The Flying Outlander" into the public domain once my research is complete.

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: After all, is not recovering this lost play and filling in a page of history heretofore missing the greater deed to do?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Well then, I suppose I should hurry back. Research and study await!

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Ah yes, here's your payment. If chance should allow it, let us meet again!

choices.text: Don't forget the part I played.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Of course. Your name will be on the title page for sure!
